A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NF2 is a mosaic condition.
NF2 mutations were detected in leukocytes in 81% (13 of 16) of inherited and 51% (46 of 91) of sporadic NF 2 patients.
the rate of detection for mutations in leukocytes is lower in sporadic NF2 cases (46%) than in inherited NF2 cases (81%), and that mosaicism in NF2 patients may account for some of the difference.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mosaicism in NF2 can result in a wide spectrum of phenotypes, including mild, severe, and even no phenotypic expression.
the presence of a mutation in a tumor does not guarantee that a patient has NF2, and that the lack of a mutation in leukocytes does not rule out the diagnosis of NF2.
mosaicism in NF2 can be quite common and that the detection of mutations in leukocytes is not a reliable method to distinguish inherited from sporadic cases.
